response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT t.tradekind AS tradekind, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM advancedbehavior a JOIN transactionrecord r ON a.translink = r.transreg JOIN trader t ON r.trdref = t.tradereg GROUP BY t.tradekind), s AS (SELECT tradekind, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM c), g AS (SELECT tradekind, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT tradekind, cnt AS behaviour_count, share, share - avg_share AS share_minus_avg FROM g WHERE avg_share IS NOT NULL AND share > avg_share

assumptions.assumption: Inner joins on exact key equality drop any behaviour record with no matching transaction or trader. Each behaviour record is counted once, because transreg and tradereg are primary keys and the joins can't duplicate rows.

A NULL tradekind forms its own group, because GROUP BY puts NULLs together. The average share is the plain average of the per-type shares, with each type weighted equally and that NULL group included. Shares are computed with floating-point division and left unrounded.
